messages:
incident-bot: ALERT — latency anomaly detected for /v1/infer (region: us-west-2). p95 jumped from ~140ms to ~920ms; p99 ~2.1s. Streaming stall rate +18% over baseline. Triggering oncall. Dashboard: https://dash.internal/redwood/infer-latency

maria (oncall): ack. I'm on it. grabbing logs and recent deploys. anyone see customer errors?

aj: seeing elevated 401/429 spikes from auth-service -> inference-gateway in the last 7m. sample: `401` downstream token-validate, and `429` on /auth/rate_check.

maria (oncall): copying logs:
```
[2024-11-02T15:12:43Z] gateway: POST /v1/infer 200 latency=0.9s
[2024-11-02T15:13:02Z] auth: rate_check 429 user=acct-XXXX quota=burst
[2024-11-02T15:13:02Z] gateway: stream stall id=svc-123 wait=700ms
```

devon: looks like control-plane auth/rate path is the choke. config-fetch also showing ~5% 5xx. maybe a configstore cold-cache. Could be a recent feature-flag change causing extra validation calls.

lisa: FYI I rolled out ff:experiment/session-probe yesterday 02:30 UTC to 30% traffic. Not aware of any changes to token flow but will pause rollout if helpful.

maria (oncall): please pause rollout @lisa — do it now. aj, can you check DB connection pools for configstore and auth DB?

aj: auth-db connection saturation: used 95% of pool on auth-primary. many short-lived queries `select token_meta` showing growth. stack traces show repeated retries from gateway.

ops-svcs: routing note — we've seen a spike of small reads to configstore for per-request feature-checks. caching TTL reduced to 0 in last deploy for fast rollouts. that exposes auth for N+1 checks.

maria (oncall): mitigation plan: 1) pause FF rollout (lisa) 2) enable local config cache fallback at gateway (devon) 3) temporarily increase auth-db pool size and open a read-replica route (aj/infra-paul) 4) relax rate-limiter from 200r/s -> 400r/s for 10m to drain backlogs. execute now and monitor p95/p99.

devon: enabling gateway local cache fallback: patching env var `FEATURE_CHECK_CACHE=on` and `CACHE_TTL=30s` on gateway canaries.

lisa: paused rollout — turned traffic for ff:experiment/session-probe -> 0%.

aj: auth-db pool increased +20 connections on primary, adding read-replica routing for non-privileged checks (will mark as eventual consistent).

infra-paul: spun up read-replica routing rule, applied iptables to allow replica access from gateway. watching replication lag — currently < 120ms.

incident-bot: Automation — applied rate-limiter temporary bump for service `gateway-auth-check` until 2419877400.

maria (oncall): monitoring metrics: p95 dropped to ~380ms after cache and rate bump; p99 down to ~1.1s but still elevated. streaming stalls reduced but not back to baseline. continuing.

devon: I can also throttle background config-checks — switching to batched validation for in-flight requests to reduce N+1. patch rolling out to 10% now.

aj: logs show fewer 429s now, auth latency median back to ~80ms. A handful of long tail DB queries still visible (slow query sample attached).

maria (oncall): customer impact: no widespread errors returned — most calls succeeded but experienced increased tail latency and some streaming rebuffering. Early signs: one enterprise tenant reported degraded streaming in support channel. tagging SRE for post-incident contact.

devon: opened temporary guardrail in gateway: if streaming stall > 800ms then fallback to shorter chunk-size. Should reduce perceived stalls for clients.

ops-svcs: note for postmortem — the reduced config cache TTL change (deploy two nights ago) likely a major contributor. That policy amplified feature-flag checks hitting auth-db.

maria (oncall): handoff in 20m to @infra-paul for follow-up and long-term remediation. current state: mitigation actions in place, metrics improving but p99 still ~800-1100ms.

infra-paul: taking over at handoff. I'll coordinate DB-side scaling plan and add circuit-breaker on per-request feature lookups.

lisa: quick summary I pushed: paused FF rollout, adding a safe default so if cache misses we don't cascade to auth for every request.

maria (oncall): creating an incident page and ticket: INC-2419876543 with timeline, customer impact, and runbook link. please add any logs or config diffs.

incident-bot: Incident page created: https://incidents.internal/INC-2419876543 — severity: Sev3 (tail latency, single-tenant support reports).

maria (oncall): final note before handoff: immediate mitigations = cache fallback + rate bump + pause rollout + read-replica. Next steps (infra): increase pool defaults, add per-request caching, postmortem to include change to cache TTL decision. I'll file the postmortem template.

infra-paul: acknowledged. I'll own long-tail remediation and coordinate with platform to revert cache TTL change or make it environment-gated. handoff complete.

lisa: adding support ticket link: https://support.redwood/customer/ABC-12345 — they reported streaming buffer spikes around 15:12 UTC.

maria (oncall): thanks all. If anything regresses ping #oncall immediately. I'll update the incident page with metrics and the mitigation timeline.

incident-bot: incident status -> Service degraded -> mitigations active -> monitoring.

maria (oncall): closing slack thread for handoff — will reopen if we see regression. postmortem owner: infra-paul.
note: This thread records a single continuous Slack thread for incident coordination: live mitigations, on-call handoff, and customer impact assessment related to inference path latency caused by DB/control-plane dependency overload.
